fediverse.sheet.step1.title: What is the fediverse?
fediverse.sheet.step1.body: The fediverse works much like email: a network of independent servers that all connect to each other. Just as a Gmail user can email someone on Outlook, apps like Mastodon and Mention can talk to each other, so people on other servers can follow you and reply to your posts.
fediverse.sheet.step2.title: How sharing works
fediverse.sheet.step2.body: When sharing is on, your public profile and posts can be seen and followed from other servers across the fediverse. Every server sets its own rules, and Mention can't control or moderate how your content appears once it leaves Mention.
fediverse.sheet.step3.title: You're always in control
fediverse.sheet.step3.body: You can turn fediverse sharing off anytime in Settings. When you do, we ask other servers to delete copies of your content. Those servers are independent, so we can't guarantee that every copy is removed.

channels.explainer.title: About channels
channels.explainer.step1.title: What is a channel?
channels.explainer.step1.body: A channel is an account that publishes on its own. Following it brings its posts to your feed without you following any of the people who write for it. That separation is what a channel is for.
channels.explainer.step2.title: It publishes, it doesn’t reply
channels.explainer.step2.body: A channel’s posts are ordinary posts: they reach feeds, search and the fediverse like anyone else’s, and you can boost one to your own profile. What you will not find is a reply box. A channel never takes replies, and that is how channels are built rather than a setting someone switched off.
channels.explainer.step3.title: Who wrote this?
channels.explainer.step3.body: A channel signs its own posts. With “Name the writer” on, the person who wrote one is shown alongside the channel; with it off, the post is the channel’s alone. That is the channel’s own choice, not something missing.

transparency.title: Transparency
transparency.heading: Who we federate with
transparency.intro: Mention is part of the fediverse — a network of independently run social sites that pass posts and follows between one another. Anyone can run one, and that openness is the point. It also means some are run by people who host things we will not carry.
transparency.introSource: This page lists every instance Mention refuses to exchange with, and why. It is rendered from the same list the server enforces, so it cannot quietly fall out of date.
transparency.whatItDoes.title: What a block does
transparency.whatItDoes.body: Nothing from a blocked instance reaches Mention. Posts, follows, likes and boosts it sends are refused as they arrive, we stop fetching its accounts and timelines, and its accounts can no longer be found or followed from here.
transparency.whatItDoes.bluntness: It applies to a whole site, not to the individual people on it. That is a blunt instrument, so we would rather use it rarely and explain it every time.
transparency.whatItDoes.scope: Each entry names one server and covers exactly that name. A subdomain is a different server — a block on example.com does not extend to social.example.com — so each one is decided on its own and appears here in its own right.
transparency.whatItDoes.limits: Worth knowing: a block governs what reaches Mention. Anything you post publicly here stays public and can still be read from anywhere, including the instances on this list.
transparency.howWeDecide.title: How a decision is taken
transparency.howWeDecide.corroboration: Most fediverse servers publish the instances they have blocked, as open data. We read several of those lists and look for the same decision reached independently by more than one of them before treating it as a signal — one server’s list is one server’s opinion, and some published blocks are contested.
transparency.howWeDecide.judgement: Corroboration is not the decision. Before anything is added we look at what we actually hold from that instance and what a block would cost the people here, and a person makes the call. Where another server’s published decision is what prompted ours, it is named below.
transparency.howWeDecide.audit: The list lives in Mention’s source code, so every entry arrives as a reviewed change carrying a date and a written reason — and can be argued with, or undone. We publish ours as open data at /federation/blocked-domains, the same way we read everyone else’s.
transparency.list.title: Instances we do not federate with
transparency.list.empty: No instances are blocked. Mention federates with the whole network today; if that changes, every decision will appear here with its reason and the date it took effect.
transparency.list.error: This list could not be loaded right now. It is served at /federation/blocked-domains if you would rather read it directly.
transparency.decidedHere: Decided from reports and moderation on Mention.
transparency.operationalBlock: Blocked urgently by an operator, ahead of a written policy entry. Its reason has not been published yet.
